content:
After Yahweh declared judgment upon the unbelieving generation, He immediately spoke of one man who stood apart from all the rest. He said, "But My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me fully. I will bring him into the land into which he went, and his descendants shall possess it" (Numbers 14:24). While an entire nation was marked by unbelief, Caleb was marked by faithfulness. It is beautiful to notice that Yahweh does not compare Caleb with the nations around him, nor even with Moses or Joshua.He compares Caleb with the rest of Israel, and He declares that Caleb had a different spirit.

What made Caleb different? It was not his strength. It was not his military skill. It was not some natural courage that the others lacked. Caleb saw the very same giants that the other spies saw. He walked through the same fortified cities.

He knew the same dangers. Yet he looked at those dangers through the promises of Yahweh instead of measuring them by human ability. The ten spies allowed their circumstances to shape their faith. Caleb allowed God’s Word to shape his understanding of the circumstances. This is the whole difference.One group looked at the giants and then decided what to believe about God. Caleb looked at God and then decided what to believe about the giants.And for this reason Yahweh said of him, "He has followed Me fully." Caleb's loyalty was complete. He did not follow Yahweh only when the journey was easy. He trusted God even when the whole multitude stood against him.While thousands chose fear, Caleb remained faithful. And because of this, God promised that Caleb would enter the land he had explored, and that his descendants would inherit it.

Then Yahweh gave another instruction. He said, "Tomorrow turn and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea" (Numbers 14:25). Only a short time earlier, Israel had stood at the very entrance of Canaan. The Promised Land was right before them. Yet because they refused to move forward in faith, Yahweh told them to turn around and go back into the wilderness. What a tragic picture this is. One day of unbelief resulted in forty years of wandering. The people who should have been advancing toward their inheritance were now retracing their steps through the desert, all because they refused to trust Yahweh at the border.

Yahweh then spoke again to Moses and Aaron. He said, "How long shall I bear with this evil congregation who grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints of the Israelites which they grumble against Me" (Numbers 14:27). Throughout their journey, Israel believed they were only complaining against Moses and Aaron. But Yahweh made it clear that every complaint against His appointed servants was truly a complaint against Him. He had heard every single word. Nothing had escaped His attention. Then Yahweh gave one of the most solemn declarations of the whole wilderness journey. He said, "As surely as I live, I will do to you exactly as I heard you say".

Now think carefully about what they had said. Earlier they had cried out, "If only we had died in Egypt, or if only we had died in this wilderness!" (Numbers 14:2). They had also asked, "Why is Yahweh bringing us into this land to fall by the sword?" (Numbers 14:3). These words, spoken in fear and unbelief, now became their very judgment. They had wished to die in the wilderness, and Yahweh declared that they would indeed die in the wilderness. They said they would never enter the land, and Yahweh declared that they would never enter the land. The very judgment they feared in their faithlessness became the judgment they received because of their unbelief. Yahweh said, "Your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness. Every one of you who was numbered, from twenty years old and upward, who has grumbled against Me, shall by no means enter the land" (Numbers 14:29-30). Only two men were excluded from this judgment, Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. The congregation had wanted to stone these two faithful men, yet Yahweh honoured the very ones whom the people had rejected.

The Israelites had also cried, "Our little ones will become plunder." They believed their children would perish if they entered Canaan. But Yahweh answered, "Your little ones, whom you said would become prey, I will bring in, and they shall know the land which you have rejected" (Numbers 14:31). How remarkable are the ways of Yahweh. The parents believed they were protecting their children through their unbelief. Instead, their unbelief kept them out of the inheritance, while the very children they feared for would one day inherit the land. The adults lost what the children gained. And Yahweh declared that Israel would wander in the wilderness for forty years, one year for each day that the spies had searched the land. During those years the nation would carry the consequences of its unbelief until the whole unbelieving generation had passed away.

Now Caleb stands before us as a beautiful example of the attitude that should mark every New Creation. The New Creation is called to have a different spirit from the spirit of this world. The world is governed by fear, doubt, unbelief, and human reasoning. But the New Creation is called to live by faith in the promises of Yahweh. Like Caleb, we will often see the very same difficulties that others see. We do not deny that giants exist. Trials, persecutions, disappointments, sickness, and hardships are all real, and faith does not pretend that these things are absent. Instead, faith looks beyond the giants and remembers the greatness of God. Caleb did not follow the majority, and neither should the New Creation measure truth by popular opinion. Even if the whole world walks in one direction, we are called to follow Christ fully.

Caleb remained loyal when others turned back, and the New Creation must also remain faithful when obedience becomes costly. We are not called to follow Christ only when the path is pleasant, but also when it is hard. Caleb waited patiently for Yahweh's promise. Although he would not receive his inheritance immediately, he never abandoned his confidence in God. In the same way, the New Creation waits patiently for every promise that God has spoken in Christ, knowing that not one of His words will ever fail. May Yahweh also be able to say of us, "My servant has a different spirit and has followed Me fully."

Israel was remembered for its complaints, but Caleb was remembered for his faithfulness. One whole generation was defined by unbelief, while one man was distinguished by wholehearted obedience. The difference between them was not their eyes, for they saw the same land. It was not their circumstances, for they walked the same road. The difference was the spirit within them.

May we not be known for our fears, our grumbling, or our excuses. May we be known instead for having a different spirit, a heart that follows Christ fully, that trusts God’s promises completely, and that remains faithful right to the very end.

title: Prayer
text:
Our Father,
Mey we have the same spirit that You saw in Your servant Caleb.

Help us to see the same giants that others see, yet to look beyond them to Your greatness.

Keep us from following the majority into fear, and teach us to follow Christ fully.

Make us loyal when obedience is costly, and patient while we wait for Your promises.

Let us not be remembered for our grumbling, but for a heart that trusts You to the end.

"But blessed are those who trust in the LORD and have made the LORD their hope and confidence." - Jeremiah 17:7

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
